newsitem.title: USA: U.S. soft red winter wheat escapes frost damage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soft red winter wheat escapes frost damage.

text.p: Attention Monday was riveted to severe damage that likely occured in portions of the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat crop but extension agronomists and cash dealers in the soft red winter region said little or no damage occured to that crop.

"It's kind of a mixed bag north of I-70 (Interstate Highway 70) but damage was not widespread and temperatures didn't get anywhere close enough to do damage in the bootheel," said Ken Kephart, extension agronomist for the University of Missouri, Columbia.
Similar scenarios were reported in other key SRW states of Ohio, Indiana and Illinois.
Kephart said Missouri's wheat crop in the southern portion of the state was at the jointing stage and "in general, north of I-70 wheat was not jointing and there was no damage."
James Beuerlein, extension agronomist for the Ohio State University, Colombus reported virtually no damage to that state's crop.
"The growing point is still pretty close to the ground in the north and it didn't get cold enough in the south to harm the crop," Beuerlein said.
Cold temperatures were noted over the weekend in northern Indiana and northern Illinois.

Also Weather Express Inc Omaha, Neb., said early Monday that the freeze line, 32 degrees Fahrenheit and below overnight Monday, would brush the northern reaches of Illinois, Indiana and Ohio. Also the northwest corner of Missouri would drop to 32 degrees F or below overnight Monday, Weather Express said.

Cash grain merchandisers in the Midwest early Monday also said there was little cause for concern for now in the SRW states. That crop was not as advanced as the hard red winter wheat crop, they said.
Also the blast of cold air did not dip into the more advanced SRW wheat plants in the southern growing region of the SRW belt.
"I think most of Indiana is all right," a cash grain merchandiser said.
